context.question: (Implied, same chapter) What is the state of the ship — lost or safe?
context.setting: A second example ship figure printed immediately after the December 1644 example; no news had been heard of the ship

attachments.key_positions: Moon lately separated from a square of Saturn, lord of the 8th and 9th, then void of course, then applying to a trine of Saturn and afterwards to opposition of Mercury, lord of the 12th and 4th, Mercury being in his detriment and entering combustion; Jupiter, dispositor of Mercury, subterranean and conjunct Mars in the term of an infortune; Mars in his fall near the cusp of the 2nd; Part of Fortune in the 6th, disposed of by retrograde afflicted Jupiter in the 2nd, and in square to both Part of Fortune and Moon; principal significator in the 4th and afflicted
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
